scope: Measures whether each generator COULD operate unmodified behind an adapter layer (a thin translation shim that reshapes a canonical entity record back into the flat per-name object shape a generator already expects) — not whether one should be built, and no adapter is designed or implemented here.
method: For each generator, its actual source-level data access pattern was inspected (per Phase 1A-2A source tracing): does it read a single flat per-entity object with consistent field names (origin_country, language, meaning, ...), or does it perform its own multi-source reconciliation logic (different access patterns per source) inside its own function bodies? The former is adapter-ready; the latter requires-refactor because an adapter can translate data shape but cannot remove reconciliation logic that exists to bridge shapes that would no longer differ.

classificationDefinitions.adapter-ready: Its current code already expects a flat object with consistent field names, or a filterable array scoped to one entity. A translation shim in front of the canonical record satisfies it with zero logic changes.
classificationDefinitions.partial: Its data access pattern is adapter-compatible, but a separate, non-adapter-solvable issue exists alongside it (e.g. two producers of the same field need one to be designated authoritative, or a pipeline-wiring question needs resolving) — the adapter question and the other issue are independent.
classificationDefinitions.requires-refactor: Its own logic performs multi-source reconciliation using source-specific access patterns (e.g. array lookups shaped differently per source). Removing the need for that reconciliation is itself a logic change an adapter cannot provide.

generators.justification: Reads record.origin_country, record.language, record.meaning, etc. — a flat per-name object. A shim producing that exact shape from a canonical record satisfies every read site without code changes. (Its rendering functions containing hardcoded fallback strings are a separate, non-adapter concern — see audit/migration-risk-register.json.)

Same flat-record access pattern as generate-programmatic-pages.js. Notably, feeding this generator canonical (enriched-equivalent) data via an adapter would ALSO structurally fix the enriched/unenriched inconsistency found in Phase 1C/1D, since the bug is which file is read, not how the generator's logic is written.

The clearest positive finding in this file: sibling-explanation-renderer.js's buildContext() does `baseRecord.origin_country || baseRecord.language || 'various origins'` — ordinary flat-field access. Routing this generator through an adapter that supplies canonical origin.country/language.primary in those same field names would eliminate the 100% sibling-page origin-fallback rate (audit/knowledge-roi.json) with ZERO changes to this generator's own code.
Its Name-Entity-side reads (first names being matched) are flat-record access; its Surname-side reads are out of this schema's scope entirely and unaffected either way.

getRank()/getMovement()/getVolatility() filter a popularity ARRAY by name_id/country/year — an adapter supplying the canonical entity's own popularity.records[] (already scoped to one name) in place of the global array satisfies these functions unchanged.
Narrow, single-field read (relatedNames.equivalents[] equivalent); trivial to satisfy via adapter.
Aggregation over a popularity array; same pattern as generate-compare-pages.js.
Same profile as generate-popularity-pages.js.

The only generator confirmed to read data/popularity.json, data/regional-trend-acceleration.json, AND data/country-differentials.json with three DIFFERENT access patterns in its own body (array filtering, by_country object keying, entries array search). An adapter can supply canonical popularity.records[]/trendAcceleration, but the reconciliation logic combining three shapes into one narrative exists specifically because those shapes differ today — under the canonical model that logic becomes dead code, not adaptable code. Removing dead logic is a refactor, not an adapter.

Data-build (producer) script. Its current output format could remain entirely unchanged if a downstream, non-generator canonicalization step assembles canonical records from its output — the producer itself needs no logic change under an adapter pattern applied to the write side.
Same producer-side reasoning as generate-country-differentials.js.
Already performs exactly the single-merge pattern the canonical model wants; its output could feed a canonical-assembly step without any change to its own merge logic.
A pure curated-data producer; unaffected by how its output is later assembled.
Deterministic rule-based producer; output format is independent of downstream assembly.
Sole producer of real popularity data; no reconciliation logic of its own.

Adapter-compatible as a producer (same reasoning as other data-build scripts), BUT it is one of two current parallel producers of variants.spellingVariants[] and pronunciation.syllableCount (alongside scripts/acquire/build-variants.js and data/names.json's own syllables field respectively). An adapter cannot decide which of two producers is authoritative — that is a design decision independent of the adapter question.
Produces a scoring ruleset, not entity data — no per-entity data shape to adapt at all.
Same dual-producer issue as normalize-names.js, from the other side of the pair.

Reads flat identity/popularity fields for its explorer grid; its own documented enriched-then-base fallback pattern would simply resolve to always finding data once fed a canonical record, with no code change required.
Consumes only identity.slug for URL construction — the simplest possible adapter case.

A pure scoring function taking already-loaded values (origin, syllables, popularity band, style) as parameters — whatever supplies those parameters (today's records, or an adapter-fed canonical entity) is invisible to this function's own logic.
Same pure-function profile as generate-sibling-harmony.js.

Adapter-compatible as a producer, but Phase 2A found its output columns (meaning_source, origin_source, confidence_score) are present-but-always-null in live data — a pipeline-connectivity question that exists independently of whether an adapter could satisfy its read/write shape.

keyFinding: 19 of 23 generators (83%) are adapter-ready — a higher proportion than the generator-impact-matrix.json complexity distribution alone would suggest, because migration COMPLEXITY (breadth of domains touched, risk of behavior change) and adapter-READINESS (can the data source be swapped without a code change) are different measurements. Several of the 5 generators classified 'high complexity' in audit/generator-impact-matrix.json (generate-programmatic-pages.js, generate-names-like.js, generate-sibling-pages.js) are nonetheless adapter-ready: their complexity comes from breadth of impact and behavior CHANGE once correct data flows through, not from any structural incompatibility with an adapter pattern.
